songs.name: It Must Have Been The Roses

ai_show_review.summary: Explosive second‑set sandwich with Terrapin, Playing jam and monster Other One
ai_show_review.blurb: The July 27 1982 Red Rocks show shines on its second set, delivering a tight Playing In The Band → Terrapin Station → Playing sandwich and a nine‑minute “Other One”. Highlights also include a blazing China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider and a soaring Stella Blue. The performance is high‑energy throughout despite some mix quirks on certain recordings.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Red Rocks on July 27, 1982 is a quintessential early‑80s Dead night where the band locks into an inspired groove right from the opening of Set 1. A solid first set builds momentum with “China Cat Sunflower” segued into “I Know You Rider”, and the extended “Sugaree” that stretches over sixteen minutes, setting up a high‑octane second half.  The centerpiece is the legendary Playing In The Band → Terrapin Station → Playing sandwich – captured in pristine mids on the top‑rated soundboard source – where Jerry’s lead lines cut through with crystalline clarity and Brent’s organ adds an urgent thrust.  A monster “Other One” (nine minutes of relentless, Phil‑driven propulsion) follows, leading into a beautifully plaintive “Stella Blue”, before the band rounds out the night with a rollicking “U.S. Blues”.  While a few recordings suffer from hiss or uneven levels, the musical chemistry is unmistakable: tight interplay, inventive bass work and a rhythm section that drives every jam forward.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard‑type source with superb midrange clarity and a balanced mix that showcases the iconic Playing > Terrapin > Playing sandwich.

key_highlights: Tight Playing In The Band → Terrapin Station → Playing sandwich captured with crystal‑clear mids
Monster nine‑minute “Other One” driven by Phil’s inventive bass lines
Blazing China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider segue that launches the night
Emotive “Stella Blue” closing the second set and a rousing “U.S. Blues” encore

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is consistently inspired – bright on the audience tapes, slightly buried in some SBD mixes but still delivering soaring phrasing throughout the Terrapin and jam sections.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides high‑energy, inventive bass that drives the “Other One” and underpins the whole second set; his “bass bombs” are a highlight.
band_performance.Bob: Weir supplies solid rhythm guitar foundation and adds a memorable scat vocal during the Playing In The Band jam, keeping the groove tight.
band_performance.Brent: Mydland’s keyboards are vibrant and propulsive, especially on Terrapin Station where his organ adds intensity; occasional mix prominence but musically essential.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart contributes dynamic fills and powerful drum breaks that propel the Rhythm Devils segment and fuel the high‑energy jams.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann locks in with Hart, delivering a steady, driving pulse throughout the set and especially during the extended improvisations.
